title: A Pharmacometric Method for Quantitative Determination of Improvement in Body Composition and Characterization of the Exposure–Response Relationship during Treatment of Obesity with Tirzepatide

citation.title: A Pharmacometric Method for Quantitative Determination of Improvement in Body Composition and Characterization of the Exposure–Response Relationship during Treatment of Obesity with Tirzepatide

printed_heading.text: CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY & THERAPEUTICS | VOLUME 118 NUMBER 6 | December 2025 1489 A Pharmacometric Method for Quantitative Determination of Improvement in Body Composition and Characterization of the Exposure–Response Relationship during Treatment of Obesity with Tirzepatide EmmanuelChigutsa*,LucyHer,XiaosuMa,ShwetaUrva andKarenSchneck About half of the world’s population is living with overweight or obesity. Tirzepatide is an approved treatment for chronic weight management. We sought to characterize the exposure–response relationship for weight reduction in patients with overweight or obesity and quantify the associated changes in body composition. Monthly body weight measurements were available from 2,539 study participants in a phase 3 clinical trial investigating placebo, 5, 10, or 15mg of tirzepatide administered once- weekly. The dependent variables used for modeling were fat- free mass (FFM) and fat mass. These FFM and fat mass values were calculated for each patient based on their total body weight, height, and sex. The exposure–response model revealed that administration of tirzepatide resulted in three times greater reduction of fat mass than that of FFM. This differential effect resulted in improved body composition over time. The model results showed good agreement with available data from a subset (10%) of clinical trial participants who had dual energy x- ray absorptiometry (DXA) measurements. For the same drug exposure, females achieved greater weight reduction than males. Study participants with higher baseline weight or body mass index at baseline had a slower rate of weight reduction and were expected to take longer to reach their nadir weight. We present and propose the use of a pharmacometric- based body composition model to describe weight reduction in future clinical trials investigating similar drugs in similar patient populations, in lieu of DXA scans. In such future trials, our approach can be used to describe exposure–response relationships, optimize doses, and investigate covariates, while considering potential differences in fat mass and FFM. Incretin- based therapies have garnered increased attention in recent years because of body weight reduction following administration of these drugs for chronic weight management.8–10 One of these drugs is tirzepatide, a glucose- dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon- like peptide- 1 receptor dual agonist.11 Tirzepatide is indicated for chronic weight management with recommended maintenance doses of 5, 10, or 15mg injected subcutaneouslyonce-weekly.Clinicaltrialsforchronicweightmanagement demonstrated 15mg tirzepatide to result in a mean decrease in body weight of more than 20% after 72weeks of treatment.8 Such magnitude of effect represents an advancement of pharmacologicalinterventiontowardchronicweightmanagement.Thisis especially so upon consideration of the fact that drugs historically indicated for obesity led to body weight reductions of about 5%12 andthatwasconsideredclinicallyrelevant.13,14 The greater weight reduction achieved with tirzepatide and other treatments can raise various questions.

endpoint.text: Stochastic simulations that included parameter variability were conducted to determine the model-predicted changes in body weight, FFM, and fat mass after 72 weeks of treatment, which was the primary endpoint in the clinical trial.

Various covariates (sex, race, age, presence/absence of nausea or vomiting or diarrhea) were assessed for their impact on baseline FFM, baseline fat mass, drug response, placebo effect, and Kout in the indirect response model.
Furthermore, since the two subcomponents were calculated from the same body weight measurement, a correlation between the residual errors for modeling each endpoint was included in the modeling.
